leads.summary: The upstream effective corner radius depends on power, but the new shell paths always use the unscaled configured radius
leads.consequence: For configured rounding=10, power=1, Hyprland window presentation uses 5 as its radius while shell surfaces cut 10; at power=4 the window uses 20 while the shell uses 10. Matching the exponent alone cannot make window and shell edges coincide. A theme actually ships power 3 (themes/solitude/hyprland.lua:19). Adjust effective radius together with power and verify short/narrow surfaces separately.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1); corroborated; published

leads.summary: Power-1 inner corner contour gives a thinner diagonal border than its requested side widths
leads.consequence: With radius=10 and uniform width=2, the outer top-left chamfer is x+y=10 but the reversed inner cut is x+y=12; their perpendicular separation is only 2/sqrt(2), around 1.41px rather than 2px. Flat/gradient border corners pinch while straight sides remain 2px. For p=1 a parallel inner diagonal needs a sqrt(2)*width shift in the cut-line intercept, rather than merely subtracting width from both radii.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2); corroborated; published

leads.summary: Open #13166 independently implements the same triangular-corner feature with incompatible Style and BorderSurface contracts
leads.consequence: Both open PRs are divergent. #13166's surface stays a Rectangle with a layer mask and `cornerChamfer`/`cornerPower`; this PR makes it an Item with `cornerRoundingPower`, no masking, and a numeric power argument where #13166 passes `chamfer` booleans. Blindly accepting either overlapping hunk drops the other's feature; they cannot both merge without selecting and reconciling the shared rendering and tests. The independent merge of their own base, this head and #13166's head produces conflicts in eight files, including BorderGeometry, Style, BorderSurface, BorderOverlay, Tray, Clipboard, Emojis, Polkit.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (gh pr view files + description); Opus self-check confirmed it covers only power <= 1; published in overlap note

leads.summary: Combining the cleanly merging #6506 refresh fix breaks this PR's kept rounding-power test
leads.consequence: #6506 wraps refresh() in an if guard. This PR's regex uses `[^}]*` after refresh's opening brace, so after the clean merge it stops at #6506's first if close and `rounding-power-test.sh` fails at 'rounding power follows the existing shell refresh lifecycle' (while the unchanged-head positive control passes). The failure is a brittle source-regex test rather than a demonstrated stale query: Quickshell queues `running=true` during an in-flight process via `targetRunning` and starts it after the current child exits. Update the test to verify refresh behavior without assuming it has no nested braces; consider the new process in #6506's guard if the intended semantics are to complete all three reads before releasing pendingRefresh.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator read #6506 refresh diff and the regex; Opus reproduced test failure on a trial merge (opus/draftcheck/review-m6506); published

leads.summary: Both open gradient-fill PRs add a FillOverlay which is circular even when this PR makes BorderSurface superelliptic
leads.consequence: #13120 and #7748 separately add gradient fills and use BorderSurface.fillSpec on popup and menu cards. Their FillOverlay invokes Geometry.roundedRectPath with no power and does not clip to the powered parent Item. Both independent BorderSurface merges have conflict markers; after a mechanical resolution retaining their FillOverlay, a configured power 1/3/4 would show a round gradient fill inside a chamfered/superellipse border (or across its cut-off corners). Any integration must pass roundingPower into FillOverlay's path or mask its fill, and test the gradient + power combination. Actual merged UI is conditional until conflicts are resolved.
leads.triage: hypothesis about resolved merge; only the verified fact (they change BorderSurface and add a round-cornered FillOverlay) published in overlap note

leads.summary: Open #7241's device-pixel border inset collides with the new CornerRectangle painter
leads.consequence: #7241 insets native and gradient strokes a device pixel to avoid fractional-scale clip loss. It replaces native Rectangle.border with a nested inset Rectangle and removes border.color/width on the surface. This PR instead inherits CornerRectangle and keeps its border.* path plus a custom-corner overlay. The three BorderSurface merge conflicts need explicit reconciliation: retaining #7241's native painter alone leaves the new powered parent fill and inset strokes with divergent outlines, while taking this PR's border code alone drops the inset fix. GitHub's MERGEABLE for #7241 is against quattro, not this divergent PR.
leads.triage: factual; verified file overlap via gh; published in overlap note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** power 2 is unchanged, power 1 draws straight chamfers on fills, and the new tests are meaningful. Compared against the base implementation, the geometry output for power 2, default and invalid powers matched on 10,110 inputs, and offscreen renders of base and head at power 2 differed in 0 pixels (software scene graph, 100% and 150% scale). `rounding_power` is read through the existing `refresh()` lifecycle, defaults to 2 and keeps the previous value on invalid readings. In-tree circles and pills (slider knob, switch track, Tailscale badge) stay circular. The border, rounding-power, button and row tests pass on the head and on the head merged into the current `quattro` tip. The head's border-geometry and rounding-power tests fail on the base. The full `test/shell` run shows the same failures, all in unrelated areas, with and without the PR (on the base and on the current tip).

The shell corners still do not match Hyprland's window corners when the power is not 2, for the two reasons below.

### Shell corners use the configured radius, but Hyprland scales it by `power / 2`

Hyprland draws windows and their borders with `rounding * (rounding_power / 2)`, not with `decoration:rounding` itself (`CWindow::rounding()` in `src/desktop/view/Window.cpp`, v0.56.2: "Make perceived roundness consistent"). The PR's curve equation matches Hyprland's, but `CornerRectangle` and `BorderSurface` pass the unscaled `Style.cornerRadius` into the geometry at every power.

| `rounding`, power | shell radius (PR) | Hyprland window radius | corner depth on the diagonal, shell / window |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10, 1 | 10 | 5 | 7.07 / 3.54 px |
| 6, 3 (bundled `solitude` theme) | 6 | 9 | 1.75 / 2.63 px |
| 10, 4 | 10 | 20 | 2.25 / 4.50 px |

**Impact:** at power 1, the case in the PR description, shell chamfers are twice as deep as window chamfers. With `solitude`, the only bundled theme with a power other than 2, shell corners become smaller than window corners, and by the diagonal-depth measure they sit further from the windows than the current circular r=6 corners (2.49 px).

**Suggested change:** apply `radius * power / 2` in one place for custom corners, for example in `CornerRectangle` or as an effective radius on `Style`. `BorderSurface`'s own `BorderOverlay` must use the same effective radius, or fill and border will not line up. `normalizeRadii` already clamps oversized results, and power 2 is unaffected.

### Borders thin out on the chamfer below power 2

`borderPaths()` builds the inner contour with radius `outer - width` and the same power. Below power 2 that band is not constant width: at power 1 the border across the chamfer is `width / sqrt(2)`.

```text
power 1, 4 px border, radius 20 (offscreen render, 100% scale)
straight edge:  4.00 px
chamfer:        2.85 px   (2.83 px at 150%)
power 2:        4.05 px on the corner
```

From the path geometry, a 1 px control border becomes about 0.71 px across a power-1 chamfer.

Hyprland corrects exactly this for window borders: `CORRECTIONOFFSET = borderSize * (sqrt(2) - 1) * max(2 - power, 0)` is subtracted from the outer border radius (`src/render/decorations/CHyprBorderDecoration.cpp`). At power 1 that keeps the chamfer band at the full border width. Above power 2 Hyprland's border is concentric like the PR's, so no change is needed there.

**Impact:** chamfered borders on panels and controls look visibly fainter on the diagonals than on the edges and than Hyprland's window borders. "Exact straight chamfers" holds for fills, not for chamfered border width.

**Suggested change:** apply an equivalent correction to the inner contour below power 2, for example inner radius `r - w + w * (sqrt(2) - 1) * max(2 - p, 0)`, per axis for per-side widths.

### `BorderSurface` is no longer a `Rectangle`

`BorderSurface` now derives from `CornerRectangle`, which is an `Item`. Its header still calls it a "Rectangle-compatible surface", and `docs/omarchy-shell.md` points surface authors to it. In an offscreen Quickshell probe and from the source:

- `BorderSurface` with `gradient: Gradient {...}`, `topLeftRadius: 4` or `border.pixelAligned: false` loads on the base but fails on the head with `Cannot assign to non-existent property`.
- A third-party circle or pill built as `BorderSurface { radius: height / 2 }` becomes a diamond (circle) or hexagon (pill) at power 1, and a superellipse-cornered shape at other powers, unless it adds `roundingPower: 2`.
- `antialiasing: false` no longer reaches the inner `Rectangle`, and a `CornerRectangle` given only `border.color` draws no border, where a `Rectangle` draws 1 px.

**Impact:** no in-tree code uses the failing properties, and every first-party circle on `BorderSurface` was pinned to power 2, so this only affects out-of-tree plugins that use these properties or circular `BorderSurface`s.

**Suggested change:** treat this as an explicit plugin API decision: update the "Rectangle-compatible surface" header comment and `docs/omarchy-shell.md` to say `BorderSurface` is no longer a `Rectangle`, and note the change for plugin authors.

**Surfaces added upstream since the base:** after merging into the current `quattro` tip, the Elsewhen plugin's native `Rectangle`s with `radius: Style.cornerRadius` stay circular while neighbouring surfaces follow the power: `shell/plugins/panels/elsewhen/CityRow.qml:48` and `shell/plugins/panels/elsewhen/Globe.qml:607`. Converting them in a rebase keeps the shell consistent.

**Optional (per-surface cost):** with custom corners, `CornerRectangle` always creates its own `BorderOverlay`, even when `border.width` is 0. Inside `BorderSurface`, which forces `border.width: 0` and draws through its own overlay, that second overlay is always built and never visible. In a single-sample probe on the software backend, a bordered surface went from 2 visual objects (base) to 13 at power 1, and creating 400 of them took 81 ms instead of 12 ms. Loading the inner `BorderOverlay` only when `root.border.width > 0` would avoid building that always-invisible overlay (3 of the 13 counted objects, plus its gradient and 10 stops); how much of the time that saves was not measured. This matters for the emoji grid, clipboard rows and calendar cells converted here.

**Out-of-range powers:** `applyRoundingPowerJson` ignores values outside [1, 10], while Hyprland clamps the shape power to [1, 10] (`CWindow::roundingPower()`). With `rounding_power = 0.5` in a Lua config, windows are chamfered but the shell keeps its previous power (circular from startup). Clamping instead of rejecting would follow the compositor.

**Overlapping open PRs:** #13166 implements the power-1 (chamfer) part of the same feature differently (it already applies `rounding * rounding_power / 2` and an even-width chamfer border) and changes `Style.qml`, `BorderGeometry.js`, `BorderSurface.qml` and `BorderOverlay.qml`. #7241, #13120 and #7748 also change `BorderSurface.qml`, and #13120 and #7748 add a `FillOverlay` that draws round-cornered gradient fills. #6506 adds an early-return `if` block to `refresh()`; combined with it, the regex in `rounding-power-test.sh` (`function refresh\(\)\s*\{[^}]*roundingPowerProc...`) stops at that block's `}` and the test fails, so the assertion is brittle, and #6506's in-flight guard would also need to cover `roundingPowerProc`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head and of Hyprland v0.56.2 source; tests run in an isolated sandbox on the merge-base, the head, the current `quattro` tip and the head merged into that tip; geometry checks and offscreen Quickshell renders compared the merge-base and the head. Renders used Qt's software scene graph without a compositor or GPU, so the GPU path is untested. Hyprland behaviour comes from its source, not a live comparison. Timing figures are single samples. Overlap with other open PRs was assessed from their diffs and trial merges of the touched files; combined branches were not run, except the #6506 test combination.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
